name: Key Contract Terms for Large Remodeling Projects in Los Angeles

mainEntity.name: What contract terms should I insist on with a general contractor in Los Angeles to protect my budget on a large remodeling project?
mainEntity.text: What contract terms should I insist on with a general contractor in Los Angeles to protect my budget on a large remodeling project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners often focus on price but overlook contract structure, which greatly affects final cost and stress. In Los Angeles, where projects and regulations are complex, a well-written contract with your general contractor is essential. First, insist on a detailed scope of work that lists materials, brands, models, and installation details wherever possible. Vague descriptions invite change orders. For items you have not selected yet, use clear allowances that realistically reflect your taste level, and document how cost differences will be handled. Change-order procedures should be specific: require written approval with pricing and time impact before extra work proceeds, except in genuine emergencies. Ask how hidden conditions—like dry rot or outdated wiring—will be identified, documented, and priced. Payment schedules should be tied to verifiable milestones, not arbitrary dates or large upfront deposits. Include retainage, if possible, to ensure completion of punch-list items. Clarify who handles permits, inspections, and any re-inspection fees. Finally, verify license, insurance, and warranty terms, and include a clear dispute-resolution path. Reviewing these points before signing can greatly improve budget control and reduce surprises during major remodeling, additions, or ADU projects.
acceptedAnswer.description: Request a detailed, itemized scope of work; clear allowance amounts for finishes; defined change-order procedures; a realistic payment schedule tied to milestones; and explicit handling of hidden conditions and contingencies. These terms make costs transparent and reduce disputes as the project unfolds.
